column4: The section's root س و ي describes a soul brought into proportion; this verse uses سَوِيًّا for the human form in which the angel appears to Mary. It is another concrete instance of the root naming a fully formed human figure.

The section names the dictionary sense of س و ي as equality and reads the leveled people as made alike. This verse calls for a كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ between communities: a shared equality of principle, which contrasts with punitive leveling that erases a people.
Before the blast leaves Thamud prostrate in 11:67, this verse says Saleh and the believers with him were saved. That survivor boundary qualifies the section's image of the community being leveled.

This verse identifies the people of al-Hijr as deniers of the messengers, the people whose secure mountain-cut homes appear in 15:82. It anchors those dwellings in the Thamud story developed by the section.
This verse pictures the earth itself shaken at the end. It extends the section's earthly leveling from punished bodies and dwellings to the ground that moves beneath them.
This verse says the earth brings out its burdens, a related judgment image to the section's fallen people and the extended earth that casts out what is within it in 84:3–4.
This verse makes the mountains become fluffed wool on the Day of Judgment. It adds another explicit Quranic scene of the terrain being undone before the section's flat plain.

This verse describes destroyed prosperous towns whose dwellings remain scarcely inhabited. It parallels the section's empty, collapsed homes and people seeming never to have lived in their settlement.

This verse pairs the destruction of Pharaoh's people's buildings with the structures they had raised. It gives a specific build-then-destroy parallel to the section's palaces and mountain homes followed by Thamud's leveling.

After 89:9 names Thamud's rock-cutting in the valley, this verse says the Lord poured punishment on the transgressing peoples named in the passage. It supplies the consequence for the ruinous landscape described there.
